page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an ARM-based Ampere Altra processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture, running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz with one thread per core. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities and memory bandwidth, alongside weaker single-core execution. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1812.89 and a multi-core score of 14472.4. Memory bandwidth tests show 563.91 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 87.42 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. While multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang perform in the average range, single-threaded tasks show limitations, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1073.0 and a weak Passmark CPU score of 6205.54. Cryptographic performance is supported by hardware AES, though the Passmark encryption test score of 1300.22 falls into the lower tier. Large language model inference is highly constrained, with text generation on a small 135M model registering at 32.29 tokens/sec.

The t2a-standard-8 offers a cost-efficient profile for scale-out workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores rather than hyperthreaded virtual cores, though it lacks advanced x86 vector extensions like AVX or AMX. This hardware profile is suited for web serving, software compilation, database operations, and multi-threaded general-purpose workloads that do not require high single-core throughput or local SSD storage.

The instance lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX but supports hardware AES cryptography. This server provides a cost-efficient option for scale-out workloads, making it suitable for web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded database operations.
